cards.claim: Higher derivative of polynomial composition at zero improves Muon optimizer convergence speed
cards.conditions: Muon optimizer with Newton-Schulz orthogonalization; NanoGPT training
cards.effect: Noticeably improves performance; Figure 5 shows faster test loss convergence
cards.evidence: Empirical convergence curves on NanoGPT; Figure 5
cards.quote: In addition, higher derivative of composition of polynomials at zero noticeably improves the performance.

cards.claim: CANS polynomial (12 matmuls) outperforms original Muon polynomial (4 iterations = 12 matmuls) at equal computational budget
cards.conditions: NanoGPT training with Muon optimizer; same total matmuls (12) per step
cards.effect: Better test loss convergence; faster per-step optimization
cards.quote: We observe, that CANS polynomial requiring 12 matmuls (purple) outperforms Muon polynomial with the same number of matmuls (4 iterations, cyan).

cards.claim: Optimized polynomial coefficients (Chebyshev-based) achieve higher derivative at zero than prior computational search variants (Jiacheng 2024) without additional matmuls
cards.conditions: Muon orthogonalization with ε-deviation tolerance; degree-3 and degree-5 polynomials
cards.effect: Same or fewer matmuls; higher polynomial derivative at origin
cards.quote: Both polynomials have higher derivative at zero than original Muon polynomial ψ(x), while requiring no more matmuls. Compositions of 9 3-rd order polynomials for ε = 0.05 (purple) and ε = 0.1 (blue) (Figure 4) also have higher derivatives than (Jiacheng, 2024) polynomial found by computational search.

cards.claim: Tolerating orthogonalization error (ε-deviation) while maximizing polynomial derivative at zero accelerates convergence of small singular values
cards.conditions: Muon optimizer; matrices with rapidly decaying singular values; Algorithm 2 (ε-orthogonalization)
cards.effect: Faster convergence without requiring SVD or exact orthogonalization
cards.quote: Polynomials with high derivatives at zero can be applied to matrices with rapidly decreasing singular values before orthogonalization (Algorithms 1, 2). This helps to speed up orthogonalization (see Figure 2).

cards.claim: Tighter deviation tolerance in Muon orthogonalization improves performance on larger models (GPT-2 medium)
cards.conditions: Muon optimizer; deviation ε from unity singular values; larger models vs small models
cards.effect: Decreased deviation improves performance; effect scales with model size
cards.evidence: Empirical observation cited from Cesista et al. 2025
cards.quote: However, further investigation suggested that decreased deviation improves the performance for larger models, e.g. GPT-2 medium (Cesista et al., 2025).

cards.claim: Newton-Schulz iteration with optimized Chebyshev coefficients converges faster than classical Newton-Schulz with fixed coefficients
cards.conditions: Matrix orthogonalization; convergence to spectral norm <1e-10; random matrices N(0,1)
cards.effect: Noticeably faster convergence in matrix multiplications (matmuls); proportional speedup in wall-clock time
cards.evidence: Empirical comparison; Figure 2 convergence curves; Table 3 matmul counts
cards.quote: We conclude that the iterations with tuned coefficients converge noticeably faster than the classical Newton-Schulz (matmuls are proportional to time, see Table 3).

cards.claim: Polynomial composition strategy (layering different degrees) achieves higher derivative at zero than single-polynomial iteration
cards.conditions: Orthogonalization with Chebyshev-optimized polynomials; multiple composition stages
cards.effect: Monotonically increasing derivative on target interval; improved convergence of small singular values
cards.quote: Using a sequence of different polynomials, rather than iterating a single one, can push singular values into the target interval more effectively and produce a faster-growing derivative at zero.
